applicabilityConditions.note: the limit is about the TMEDA.(BH3)2 adduct's lability, so it applies to any catalysed HBpin hydroboration that uses TMEDA inhibition as its evidence of true catalysis
applicabilityConditions.reaction: hydroboration of terminal alkynes and alkenes with pinacolborane in toluene (and diglyme), BH3 at 20 mol %
applicabilityConditions.substratesNotCovered: carbonyl compounds, for which the TMEDA test is not compatible (SI Section S4)
applicabilityConditions.temperatures: external heating-block temperatures; room temperature about 18 °C
applicabilityConditions.tmedaLoading: one-to-one TMEDA to 'catalyst' for the headline; 0.5 to 1.0 eq extends inhibition but not completely

confidence.basis: two runs per entry; the authors note BH3 generated in situ is far below the nominal catalyst concentration, so the loading needed in a real test is uncertain

cost.note: bench-scale NMR kinetics; runs are the average of two; no monetary cost reported

entities.label: TMEDA inhibition test for hidden BH3 catalysis in HBpin hydroboration

outcomeSummary: Alkyne: 0.5 eq TMEDA gives less than 5 % product at 80 and 100 °C. Alkene: 70 % at 0.5 eq and 80 °C; 11, 9 and 7 % at 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0 eq at 100 °C. The authors conclude false negatives remain possible.
